title: Polynomial-time simulation of a counter program
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program with a finite label set $Lambda$ and decidable equality on labels, and fix a start label $l_0\inLambda$. Let $f$ map binary strings to binary strings, and let $C,c\inmathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary input $x$, there is a time $t\le C(|x|+1)^c$ at which the run of $P$ from its initial state at $l_0$ has halted and has output $f(x)$. Then $f$ is computable by a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine in time $C' (n+1)^{c'}$ on every input of length $n$, for some natural numbers $C',c'$.
hypotheses_covered: The label set is finite and has decidable equality
A function $f$ from binary strings to binary strings
For every input $x$, a time $t\le C(|x|+1)^c$ with halted run and output $f(x)$
replaced: Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ natural-number registers with a finite set of labels $\Lambda$, i.e.\ an assignment to each label of one instruction (halt, jump, print a bit, increment a register, decrement a register saturating at $0$, branch on a register being zero, print the value $v$ of a register as $1^v$, or read and consume the next input bit, branching on end-of-input, $0$ or $1$). Fix a start label $\ell_0 \in \Lambda$, a function $f : \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ and constants $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose that for every input $x \in \{0,1\}^*$ there is some $t \le C(|x|+1)^c$ such that running $P$ on $x$ for $t$ steps from the initial state (label $\ell_0$, all registers $0$, no input read, empty output) reaches a halted state whose output is $f(x)$. Then $f$ is polynomial-time computable: some finite binary-alphabet Turing machine computes $f$ within $C'(n+1)^{c'}$ steps on every input of length $n$, for some constants $C', c' \in \mathbb{N}$.
